title: Signal cartography: quick-stitched requests and implementation seeds
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick, stitch-together synthesis of recurring runtime and API asks surfaced over May->Jun 2024 from frontline CS, a few enterprise pilot threads, and runtime ops. Goal: identify fast patches (<=2w) vs. medium bets (1-2 sprints) vs. research asks; call out clear owner candidates. This is not exhaustive — use as a launchpad for a prioritized spike list.

Topline summary (TL;DR)
- Recurring customer pain: intermittent latency spikes on long-chat sessions (mostly customers using streaming + large context).
- Surface-level causes reported by customers: token-level stalls, KV cache staleness after model rollouts, and per-request cold starts during regional failover.
- Most requested features: predictable per-request latency SLOs, configurable fallback to smaller quantized variants, and a simple dashboard view showing cache hit ratio per route.

Representative customer quotes
- "We see 2–3s pauses mid-stream every few thousand tokens; hard to repro in dev — happens in production at scale." — Fintech pilot (acct: FinEdge) 2024-05-22
- "If we could opt into a lower-quality but faster model under load it's a win — right now our app times out." — Enterprise legal search (acct: LexMap) 2024-06-01

Observed signals and data points (ops + CS)
- Traces: SRE tracing shows small tail latencies concentrated where KV-cache lookup falls back to disk (~6% of requests in NA region last 30 days). See GH PR/trace links above.
- Metrics: Route-level p99 increased from 320ms -> 780ms for long-chat route during canary rollout on 2024-05-30.
- Customer bug reports: ~14 unique accounts flagged similar mid-stream stalls in May (CS ticket log).

Stitched requests (clusters and examples)
1) Latency stalls on long sessions
- Ask: reduce mid-stream stalls; surface clear troubleshooting signals in the Console.
- Workaround customers used: client-side heuristics to chop sessions into shorter requests; loses state and increases tokens/cost.
- Quick patch (<=2w): Console: add a per-route "recent stall events" banner + sample trace link (owner: observability eng).
- Medium effort (1 sprint): runtime: add a guard to prioritise KV-cache in-memory hotset after rollouts (owner: serving-runtime).
- Research (2–4 sprint): kernel-level queue analysis for continual batching pressure.

2) Need for predictable fallback policies
- Ask: automatic fallback toggles to quantized model variants when latency SLO breached for N minutes.
- Customer benefit: maintain degraded but responsive service instead of timeouts.
- Quick patch: document recommended manual config (dedicated plan) + provide an example rollout policy file in Templates (owner: product-hosted-api + docs).
- Medium patch: API flag to enable "auto-fallback" with simple thresholds (owner: platform-engineering + serving-runtime).

3) Visibility: cache hit ratio and route-level KV metrics
- Ask: a dashboard tile showing KV cache hits/misses per route and last model rollout timestamp.
- Why: ops teams want to correlate stalls with rollouts/cold starts.
- Quick patch: export aggregate metric to console (observability team) and add a CSV download for route owners.

4) Billing surprises from automatic batching
- Ask: customers confused about sudden token bill increases when batching changed. Need better billing attribution.
- Quick patch: add a short blurb in invoices and console explaining batching heuristics and when it affects per-token accounting (owner: finance + console).

Priority rubric (suggested)
- Urgency: number of accounts impacted x severity (timeouts > minor slowdowns) x revenue/contract status.
- Low-friction wins (high impact/low cost): Console visibility, billing explanations, rollout policy templates.
- Medium bets: auto-fallback, KV in-memory hotset guard.
- Research long-term: kernel scheduling and batching fairness for mixed tenant workloads.

Proposed next actions (owner suggestions)
- Week 0: CS to create a canonical incident thread with 10 representative tickets and link traces (owner: Asha).
- Week 1: Observability to add "stall event" banner in Console prototype; share mock (owner: Claire).
- Week 2: Product + Platform to draft simple "fallback policy" JSON config + docs snippet for Dedicated customers (owner: Jordan).
- Sprint 2: Serving-runtime to schedule spike on KV in-memory hotset guard; produce perf microbench.

Notes / open questions
- How often do rollouts cause cache invalidation? Is it model-variant-only or any config change? (SRE/serving-runtime question).
- Is auto-fallback safe for customers with strict quality requirements (legal, healthcare)? We need an allowlist.
- Can we simulate customer workloads for the kernel-batching research without needing production traffic? (possible: synthetic load harness in infra/temp).

Attachments and artifacts
- Link to sample trace: GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412
- Example fallback policy (work-in-progress): CONFLUENCE: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=9876543
- Representative CS tickets: JIRA INF-736, INF-741, INF-782 (see linked list)

Notes to self
- Keep this doc short. Move canonicalized findings into Confluence when we have triage outcomes.
- Schedule 30m sync with Claire + Jordan end of week to confirm owners and immediate next steps.

Rough customer impact estimate (back-of-envelope)
- If quick visibility changes deployed, we expect reduction in duplicate CS escalations by ~40% (fewer unknowns).
- Auto-fallback prototype could reduce hard timeouts for affected accounts by ~65% at the cost of downshifted quality. Need to validate via A/B.

End of note.

(rough, patched-up; intended as a working artifact — comments welcome)
